title: Annotatio III §.VIII: Better theologians grow milder; magistrates filled with desire for ecclesiastical peace
pass_a_gloss: For besides that the better Theologians of either Party have grown accustomed thereafter to feel more mildly and kindly about themselves mutually and their Sects, and by their examples have led their hearers to do the same; so they have filled their Magistrates more and more with love and desire of reconciling Ecclesiastical Peace.
pass_b_english: For besides this: the better theologians on both sides grew used to thinking more mildly and kindly of one another and of their own parties, and by example led their hearers to do the same;
so they filled their magistrates more and more with love and desire for reconciling church peace.
source_text: Nam praeterquàm quòd meliores utriusque Partis Theologi, mitius dehinc benigniusque de se mutuo Sectisque suis, sentire assuevêre, auditoresque suos ad idem faciendum, exemplis suis induxêre; ita Magistratus suos amore ac desiderio Pacis Ecclesiasticae conciliandae magis magisque implevêre.

lemmas.gloss: of one another and their parties

notes: Mitigation of party feeling + magistrates; before Post Lipsiacum.
